history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: His family is put with Black Partridge's village, on the south side of the Illinois River, opposite the head of Peoria Lake, one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
He is of the Sturgeon gens (N′-mă′), and his children are of it after him.
The winter before, he hunted with his family on the Kankakee and traded the skins at Kinzie's for powder, cloth and kettles.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

paragraphs: His family is put with Black Partridge's village, on the south side of the Illinois River, opposite the head of Peoria Lake, one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
He is of the Eagle gens (K′-nou′), and his children are of it after him.
He has a pony, and some winters went as far as the Wabash to hunt.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

Sunawchewome made his mark on the treaty of Portage des Sioux, 18 July 1815, the peace of the Illinois River Potawatomi with the United States: the one record of him we have. Everything else here is reconstructed.
